description: The outbound chat envelope. Derived from packages/core/src/engine.ts `send(text, extra?)` and the send/extras tests in packages/core/tests/engine.test.ts. The producer side of this wire is clg_pp_payment `vm-mirror/wav2lip-training/home/azureuser/livealman-host/host.py` (origin/staging) — `parse_pp_chat` validates exactly this shape off LiveKit's `lk.chat` text stream. The rule the vectors exist to hold: the envelope is built ENGINE-SIDE, and `extra` is merged FIRST so the engine's own fields always win. A host cannot forge `request_id`, downgrade `v`, or substitute the text the user actually typed — flip the merge order and every no-clobber row below fails. `request_id` is minted fresh per turn and therefore cannot be pinned to a literal: rows assert it against `expect.requestId` instead (`pattern` names the format, `notEqualTo` lists values an extra tried to inject, and `uniqueAcrossBuilds` means a runner builds the row TWICE and the two ids must differ). `expect.envelope` is compared against the built envelope with `request_id` removed. `uuid-v4` is what the shipped engine mints; the RECEIVER's constraint is looser (host.py `_REQUEST_ID_RE` is `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,96}$`), so an implementation that wants a different id scheme is changing this contract deliberately rather than working around it. `ready` DEFAULTS TO true: a row omitting it is built on a session whose renderer has settled. Set it to false to exercise the send guard, which throws the typed `not-ready` error rather than publishing. NOTE on extras and the receiver: the engine passes any extra through, but PP's host allowlists {v, request_id, text, gamification_level, avatar_state_block} and rejects an envelope carrying anything else. That is a receiver policy, not an engine one — the engine is the wrong place to hardcode one deployment's allowlist — so the rows below pin construction, and the two PP-real extras appear as the worked example.

cases.name: extras_cannot_clobber_v_request_id_or_text
cases.comment: The whole reason the merge order is what it is. A host that sets these keys gets its OWN values discarded, not the engine's.

cases.name: the_two_penthouse_extras_ride_along_unchanged
cases.comment: host.py `parse_pp_chat` accepts exactly these two beyond the engine's own three. gamification_level is a non-negative integer; avatar_state_block is a string.

cases.name: nested_extras_are_carried_through_structurally
cases.comment: The merge is one level deep; values are passed by reference, not rebuilt.

cases.name: text_is_passed_through_verbatim
cases.comment: No trimming, no normalization, no escaping beyond JSON. Whitespace and non-BMP characters are the user's, and the receiver is what decides whether an all-whitespace turn is legal.

cases.name: send_before_the_renderer_is_ready_is_refused
cases.comment: A turn published into a room whose renderer has not painted is a reply nobody sees. The guard is on the session, not on the envelope, so it is pinned here rather than left to the host.
